advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm a retryably-abandoned candidate with a time-less event (eventCreatedOn/createdOn absent → ev_time 0) cannot be silently dropped from the hold-back, or document/handle it explicitly.
evidence: src/rebar/review_bot/reconcile.py:330: `floors = [t for t in held_back.values() if t > 0]`
reconcile.py:328-329 comment: "Ignore time-less (0) candidates: they carry no usable bound, and clamping to 0 would rescan the entire retained log every pass."

_event_time falls back to patchSet.createdOn then 0 (reconcile.py:129-143), so a candidate lacking both eventCreatedOn and patchSet.createdOn yields ev_time=0 and is dropped from the hold-back despite being owed a vote
advisory.finding: A retryably-abandoned candidate whose normalized event carries no usable time (eventCreatedOn resolves to 0) is silently excluded from the hold-back: `floors = [t for t in held_back.values() if t > 0]` drops it, so the cursor advances to `newest` and that candidate falls outside all future windows — the exact never-retried failure mode bug 9f63 fixes, just narrower to time-less events.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the carried eventCreatedOn for the winning patchset is the correct time to clamp to regardless of events-log ordering.
evidence: src/rebar/review_bot/reconcile.py:192-199: `if prev is None or num >= prev_num:` then stores `"eventCreatedOn": _event_time(ev)`
docstring reconcile.py:158-160 claims the event 'CARRIES ITS eventCreatedOn FORWARD ... needs each candidate's own event time to clamp back to'
advisory.finding: _candidate_events keeps the highest patchset (`num >= prev_num`, ties overwrite in iteration order) but stores that winning event's own eventCreatedOn; if the events-log is not ordered newest-last, the carried time for a held-back candidate may not be its earliest occurrence — the hold-back clamp is then to a later time than strictly necessary. Re-admission still works (inclusive re-fetch of the same event), but the low-water mark can be less conservative than the docstring implies.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a reconcile test where has_llm_review_vote raises GerritError on a NON-newest candidate and assert the candidate is re-driven next pass (cursor held back).
evidence: ReconcileGerrit.has_llm_review_vote (test_review_bot.py:704-706) returns `revision in self._voted` and never raises per-candidate GerritError
The new tests exercise only the timeout branch (asyncio.sleep(3600)) and voter status branches (error/deferred/voted/post_vote_closed), not the has_llm_review_vote check-error branch
advisory.finding: The check-error hold-back branch (cursor held back when has_llm_review_vote raises GerritError) is untested. This is one of the three retryable-abandonment reasons the diff centrally introduces (the docstring lists 'an events-log check error, a review timeout, or a voter error/deferred'), and it has its own code path setting held_back[change_id]=ev_time, but no test injects a per-candidate GerritError from has_llm_review_vote — the ReconcileGerrit double's has_llm_review_vote never raises. A regression that dropped the held_back assignment in this branch would not be caught.
scenarios: A future refactor drops or misroutes the held_back assignment in the GerritError handler; a candidate whose vote-existence check errors is silently skipped past the cursor and never retried — the exact class of defect 9f63 fixes.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend ReconcileGerrit to raise GerritError for a designated change_id (e.g. a check_error_revisions set) and add a test mirroring test_reconcile_cursor_holds_back_an_abandoned_non_newest_candidate for the check-error path.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In the poison-pill test, capture logs and assert a RECONCILE_DEGRADED record with reason=holdback_expired naming the doomed change_id is emitted.
evidence: reconcile.py:334-340: `if oldest < ceiling:` ... `_degraded("holdback_expired", change_ids=..., oldest_held_back=..., max_holdback_seconds=...)`
test docstring (test_review_bot.py:2037): 'the cursor advances and the change is surfaced as ``holdback_expired``.' — but the test body asserts only `cursor >= reconcile._to_t1(4900)`
search 'holdback_expired' in tests returned only the docstring line 2037, no assertion on emitted marker/log record
reconcile.py:98-100: _degraded emits 'RECONCILE_DEGRADED ' + json — a greppable observability contract this change relies on to surface stuck changes
advisory.finding: The poison-pill test does not assert the RECONCILE_DEGRADED reason=holdback_expired marker is emitted, though the diff makes emitting it an explicit contract ('when the ceiling releases a still-failing candidate we emit the greppable degraded marker so the change is surfaced loudly instead of being dropped in silence'). The test asserts only the cursor value (>= 4900); the observability half of the contract (the greppable marker with change_ids/oldest_held_back) is untested, so a regression that advances the cursor but drops the _degraded('holdback_expired', ...) emission would pass green.
scenarios: A refactor drops the _degraded('holdback_expired') call while still clamping the cursor; the stuck change is silently dropped exactly as before, defeating the 'surfaced loudly' guarantee, and the suite stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Wrap the reconcile_once call in caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING, ...) and assert a record with 'RECONCILE_DEGRADED' and '"reason": "holdback_expired"' listing 'rebar~main~Idoom' in change_ids.
